newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - SEPT 13.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - SEPT 13.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:

- Hungarian Prime Minister and Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar will meet in Slovakia this evening in the CEFTA prime ministerial summit. They might discuss also the issue of the Bos-Nagymaros dam.

- The Hungarian government will grant health equipment worth one million forints to help reconstruction in Bosnia, as decided late last year and wishes to participate also in the future in the reconstruction of the country.
- Foreign Ministry Secretary of State Ferenc Somogyi denied that the West put pressure on the two countries in respect of the Hungarian-Romanian basic treaty.
- Before the signing of the Hungarian-Romanian basic treaty the Hungarian parliament's foreign affairs committee will discuss the document and also the site of the signing.

- Little progress has been achieved since the Taiwanese government six years ago promised to participate in eastern European investments. Hungary hopes that the current visit of a Taiwanese delegation now visiting Hungary will give a boost business relations.
- The delegation of the International Monetary Fund will arrive in Hungary in the near future.
